label: Consent
say: Hello, and welcome. I am a virtual assistant for the office of attorney Pankaj Raval. I am not the attorney or a real person; I am an artificial intelligence program that uses his likeness. This conversation will be recorded and transcribed so that attorney Raval can review it. What I explain is general information, not legal advice. Do you agree to have this conversation recorded? Please say yes or no.

label: Conflict check
say: Thank you. Before we go on, the office must check that there is no conflict of interest. For now, please tell me only names: your full name, your spouse's or partner's name, and the names of the other people who would be part of your plan, such as your children, the people you would leave things to, or who would care for your children. Please do not tell me details about your property or your wishes yet.

label: What a trust is
say: Thank you. Today I will explain, step by step, how a living trust is created in California. A revocable living trust is a legal document in which you place your property in the name of the trust. You keep full control while you are alive, and you can change it or cancel it whenever you want. When you pass away, the person you chose delivers the property to your heirs, without going through the court.

label: Why do it
say: Why does this matter in California? Because here, when a person dies with property above a certain value in their name alone, for example a house, the family normally has to go through a court process called probate. That process often takes a year or more, has costs set by law that can run to thousands of dollars, and is public. A properly made trust generally avoids that process. Attorney Raval will confirm the current limits and whether a trust makes sense in your case.

label: Step 1: type of trust
say: Step one: decide the type of trust. A single person makes an individual trust. A married couple normally makes a joint trust, because in California most of what is acquired during the marriage belongs to both spouses.

label: Step 2: inventory
say: Step two: make a list of what you own. Houses and land, bank accounts, investments, businesses, vehicles, life insurance and retirement accounts. Not everything goes into the trust in the same way, but the attorney needs to see the whole picture.

label: Step 3: people
say: Step three: choose the people. You are normally the first trustee, meaning the person who manages the property. Then you choose a successor trustee, the trusted person who will take your place if you pass away or become incapacitated. And you choose your beneficiaries: who receives what, when and how. For example, you can decide that your children receive their share at a certain age, and not all at once.

label: Step 4: drafting and signing
say: Step four: draft and sign the document. The attorney prepares the trust with your instructions. You review it, and you sign it, normally in front of a notary public.

label: Step 5: transfer the assets
say: Step five, and it is the most important one: transfer your property into the trust. An empty trust protects nothing. For your house, a new deed in the name of the trust is prepared and recorded at the county recorder's office. Moving your house into your own revocable trust normally does not change your property taxes. Bank and investment accounts are changed to the name of the trust at each institution. Retirement accounts and life insurance are generally not transferred; instead, you review who you named as beneficiary.

label: Step 6: supporting documents
say: Step six: the documents that go with the trust. A pour-over will, which sends into the trust any property that was left out, and where you name a guardian for minor children. A power of attorney, so someone can handle your finances if you cannot. And an advance health care directive, so someone you trust can make medical decisions for you.

label: Step 7: keep it current
say: Step seven: keep it up to date. Review your trust when there is a major change: a marriage, a divorce, a birth, a death, or when you buy or sell property. New property should be bought in the name of the trust.

label: Questions for the attorney
say: That is the whole process. What questions do you have for attorney Raval about your situation? Tell me now and he will answer them.

label: Contact
say: What is your full name, and the best phone number or email address to reach you?

label: Closing
say: Thank you very much. Attorney Raval will review this conversation and his office will contact you. Remember that this was general information; the attorney will give you the recommendation for your case. Have a wonderful day.
